1	# DarkIRC Channel for IronClaw — Build & Maintenance Guide
2	
3	## Directory Layout
4	
5	```
6	~/ironclaw/                          ← IronClaw repo (main binary)
7	├── wit/
8	│   └── channel.wit                  ← WASM channel interface definition
9	├── src/
10	│   └── tools/wasm/
11	│       └── host.rs                  ← Patched: localhost HTTP allowed
12	├── channels-src/
13	│   └── darkirc/                     ← DarkIRC channel project
14	│       ├── build.sh
15	│       ├── Cargo.toml               ← [workspace] at end, wit-bindgen = "0.36"
16	│       ├── darkirc.capabilities.json
17	│       ├── src/
18	│       │   └── lib.rs               ← WASM channel source
19	│       └── adapter/
20	│           ├── darkirc_adapter.py   ← IRC-to-HTTP bridge (Python, no deps)
21	│           ├── darkirc-adapter.service
22	│           └── Containerfile
23	└── target/release/ironclaw          ← Main binary (rebuild only for ironclaw patches)
24	
25	~/.ironclaw/                         ← IronClaw runtime data
26	├── .env                             ← Bootstrap config (DATABASE_BACKEND, LLM_*, etc.)
27	├── ironclaw.db                      ← SQLite database (workspace, pairing, history)
28	└── channels/
29	    ├── darkirc.wasm                 ← Compiled WASM channel (copied after build)
30	    └── darkirc.capabilities.json    ← Channel config (copied after changes)
31	```
32	
33	## What Lives Where
34	
35	| Thing | Location | When to touch |
36	|-------|----------|---------------|
37	| WASM channel source | `channels-src/darkirc/src/lib.rs` | Changing channel behavior |
38	| Capabilities JSON | `channels-src/darkirc/darkirc.capabilities.json` | Changing permissions, polling, allowlist |
39	| Adapter source | `channels-src/darkirc/adapter/darkirc_adapter.py` | Changing IRC behavior, message limits |
40	| Installed WASM | `~/.ironclaw/channels/darkirc.wasm` | Never edit directly — copy from build |
41	| Installed capabilities | `~/.ironclaw/channels/darkirc.capabilities.json` | Never edit directly — copy from source |
42	| IronClaw localhost patch | `src/tools/wasm/host.rs` line ~265 | Only if ironclaw repo is reset/updated |
43	
44	## Build: WASM Channel Only (most common)
45	
46	After editing `src/lib.rs`, `Cargo.toml`, or `darkirc.capabilities.json`:
47	
48	```bash
49	cd ~/ironclaw/channels-src/darkirc
50	cargo build --target wasm32-wasip2 --release
51	cp target/wasm32-wasip2/release/darkirc_channel.wasm ~/.ironclaw/channels/darkirc.wasm
52	cp darkirc.capabilities.json ~/.ironclaw/channels/
53	```
54	
55	Then restart ironclaw. No need to rebuild the main binary.
56	
57	### Common build errors
58	
59	**"current package believes it's in a workspace"**
60	```bash
61	echo '[workspace]' >> Cargo.toml
62	```
63	
64	**"can't find library darkirc_channel"**
65	Make sure `Cargo.toml` and `src/lib.rs` are at the same level — not inside a `channel/` subdirectory.
66	
67	**wit_bindgen path errors**
68	The path in `lib.rs` must resolve from `Cargo.toml` location to `~/ironclaw/wit/channel.wit`:
69	```rust
70	wit_bindgen::generate!({
71	    world: "sandboxed-channel",
72	    path: "../../wit/channel.wit",  // from channels-src/darkirc/ → wit/
73	});
74	```
75	
76	## Build: IronClaw Binary (rare)
77	
78	Only needed when patching IronClaw itself (e.g., the localhost HTTP fix in `host.rs`):
79	
80	```bash
81	cd ~/ironclaw
82	cargo build --release
83	```
84	
85	This takes a while. The binary lands at `~/ironclaw/target/release/ironclaw`.
86	
87	### The Localhost HTTP Patch
88	
89	IronClaw's WASM sandbox blocks plain HTTP. Our patch in `src/tools/wasm/host.rs` (~line 265) allows it for localhost:
90	
91	```rust
92	let validator = AllowlistValidator::new(capability.allowlist.clone());
93	// Allow plain HTTP for localhost/loopback endpoints
94	let validator = if capability.allowlist.iter().any(|p| p.host == "127.0.0.1" || p.host == "localhost" || p.host == "::1") {
95	    validator.allow_http()
96	} else {
97	    validator
98	};
99	```
100	
101	If you pull upstream changes to ironclaw, check if this patch survives. If `host.rs` was modified upstream, you may need to re-apply it.
102	
103	## Running
104	
105	### 1. Start the adapter
106	
107	```bash
108	# Direct
109	DARKIRC_NICK=kageho python3 ~/ironclaw/channels-src/darkirc/adapter/darkirc_adapter.py
110	
111	# Or via systemd user service
112	cp ~/ironclaw/channels-src/darkirc/adapter/darkirc-adapter.service ~/.config/systemd/user/
113	# Edit the service file: set DARKIRC_NICK, paths, etc.
114	systemctl --user daemon-reload
115	systemctl --user enable --now darkirc-adapter
116	```
117	
118	The adapter connects to DarkIRC on `localhost:6667` and listens for HTTP on `localhost:6680`.
119	
120	### 2. Start IronClaw
121	
122	```bash
123	# Using the start script (loads env vars)
124	~/ironclaw/start_ironclaw.sh
125	
126	# Or manually
127	cd ~/ironclaw
128	source ~/.ironclaw/.env
129	source .ironclaw.env  # if you have extra vars here
130	HTTP_PORT=9098 HTTP_WEBHOOK_SECRET="your-secret" ./target/release/ironclaw
131	```
132	
133	### 3. Verify
134	
135	Check ironclaw startup logs for:
136	```
137	Added channel: darkirc
138	```
139	
140	And polling activity:
141	```
142	Polling tick - calling on_poll channel=darkirc
143	```
144	
145	Test the adapter directly:
146	```bash
147	curl http://127.0.0.1:6680/health
148	curl http://127.0.0.1:6680/poll
149	```
150	
151	## Adapter Environment Variables
152	
153	| Variable | Default | Description |
154	|----------|---------|-------------|
155	| `DARKIRC_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | DarkIRC IRC server |
156	| `DARKIRC_PORT` | `6667` | DarkIRC IRC port |
157	| `DARKIRC_NICK` | `kageho-bridge` | Bot nick on IRC |
158	| `ADAPTER_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | HTTP listen address |
159	| `ADAPTER_PORT` | `6680` | HTTP listen port |
160	| `ADAPTER_SECRET` | (empty) | Bearer token (optional) |
161	| `ADAPTER_MAX_QUEUE` | `500` | Max buffered messages |
162	| `ADAPTER_LOG_LEVEL` | `INFO` | Log verbosity |
163	
164	## Capabilities JSON Reference
165	
166	The file at `~/.ironclaw/channels/darkirc.capabilities.json` must match IronClaw's expected schema exactly. Known working version:
167	
168	```json
169	{
170	  "type": "channel",
171	  "name": "darkirc",
172	  "description": "DarkIRC P2P anonymous IRC channel via local HTTP adapter",
173	  "setup": {
174	    "required_secrets": []
175	  },
176	  "capabilities": {
177	    "http": {
178	      "allowlist": [
179	        { "host": "127.0.0.1", "path_prefix": "/" },
180	        { "host": "localhost", "path_prefix": "/" }
181	      ],
182	      "rate_limit": {
183	        "requests_per_minute": 60,
184	        "requests_per_hour": 3000
185	      }
186	    },
187	    "secrets": {
188	      "allowed_names": []
189	    },
190	    "channel": {
191	      "allowed_paths": [],
192	      "allow_polling": true,
193	      "min_poll_interval_ms": 3000,
194	      "workspace_prefix": "channels/darkirc/",
195	      "emit_rate_limit": {
196	        "messages_per_minute": 100,
197	        "messages_per_hour": 5000
198	      }
199	    }
200	  },
201	  "config": {
202	    "adapter_url": "http://127.0.0.1:6680",
203	    "dm_policy": "pairing",
204	    "allow_from": [],
205	    "poll_interval_seconds": 3
206	  }
207	}
208	```
209	
210	### Schema gotchas
211	
212	- `"http"` must be an object with `allowlist`, NOT a boolean
213	- `"secrets"` must be `{"allowed_names": [...]}`, NOT a string array
214	- `"channel"` must include `allow_polling`, `workspace_prefix`, `emit_rate_limit`
215	- `"required_secrets"` must be `[]` (empty array) unless you actually use secrets
216	- Do NOT include `"credentials"` unless you match the exact sub-schema (has a required `name` field)
217	
218	## Pairing
219	
220	DM policy in `config.dm_policy`:
221	- `"open"` — anyone can message
222	- `"allowlist"` — only nicks in `config.allow_from` array
223	- `"pairing"` — unknown senders get a code, approve via CLI
224	
225	```bash
226	# List pending pairing requests
227	ironclaw pairing list darkirc
228	
229	# Approve a user
230	ironclaw pairing approve darkirc CODE123
231	
232	# Pre-approve nicks in capabilities JSON
233	"allow_from": ["sun", "cmcsunmoon"]
234	```
235	
236	Pairing approvals survive restarts (stored in database). They do NOT survive `ironclaw onboard` (which can wipe the database).
237	
238	## Message Splitting
239	
240	Long agent responses are split into IRC-sized chunks. The limit is in `src/lib.rs`:
241	
242	```rust
243	let chunks = split_message(&response.content, 450);
244	```
245	
246	And in the adapter `darkirc_adapter.py`:
247	
248	```python
249	for chunk in [text[i:i+450] for i in range(0, len(text), 450)]:
250	```
251	
252	DarkIRC enforces ~512 byte IRC line limit. After protocol overhead, ~450 chars is the safe max. The `split_message` function breaks at newlines and spaces, and handles multi-byte UTF-8 safely.
253	
254	## Troubleshooting
255	
256	### "HTTP request not allowed: Denied(InsecureScheme)"
257	The localhost HTTP patch in `host.rs` is missing. Re-apply it and rebuild ironclaw.
258	
259	### "Invalid capabilities JSON"
260	Schema mismatch. Replace `~/.ironclaw/channels/darkirc.capabilities.json` with the known working version above.
261	
262	### "WASM on_respond call failed" (trap/panic)
263	Usually a UTF-8 slicing issue in `split_message`. Make sure you're using the version with `is_char_boundary` checks.
264	
265	### Channel shows "installed=yes active=no"
266	- Is the adapter running? (`curl http://127.0.0.1:6680/health`)
267	- Check ironclaw startup logs for darkirc errors
268	- Re-copy both `.wasm` and `.capabilities.json` to `~/.ironclaw/channels/`
269	
270	### Approval flow broken over DarkIRC
271	Tool approval over IRC is flaky. Auto-approve is the pragmatic workaround:
272	```bash
273	ironclaw config set agent.auto_approve true
274	```
275	
276	### Database wiped by onboard
277	`ironclaw onboard` can destroy your database and `.env`. NEVER re-run it casually. Back up first:
278	```bash
279	cp ~/.ironclaw/ironclaw.db ~/.ironclaw/ironclaw.db.bak
280	cp ~/.ironclaw/.env ~/.ironclaw/.env.bak
281	```
282	
283	## Workspace Memory
284	
285	Stored in SQLite (`~/.ironclaw/ironclaw.db`), not filesystem.
286	
287	```bash
288	# List workspace files
289	ironclaw memory tree
290	
291	# Read a file
292	ironclaw memory read SOUL.md
293	
294	# Write a file
295	ironclaw memory write SOUL.md < ~/SOUL.md
296	
297	# Write inline
298	ironclaw memory write config/gotify.md << 'EOF'
299	Gotify endpoint: http://192.168.1.157:8080
300	Gotify API token: your-token
301	EOF
302	```
303	
304	The agent cannot write to protected paths like `SOUL.md` directly (security policy). Use the CLI.

# XMPP WASM Channel

This directory contains the installable `xmpp` WASM channel package.

It is the IronClaw-facing adapter layer for XMPP:

- `xmpp.wasm` is installed into `~/.ironclaw/channels/`
- `xmpp.capabilities.json` defines setup secrets, setup fields, and HTTP permissions
- the channel talks to a local `xmpp-bridge` process over loopback HTTP

The actual XMPP protocol session, MUC membership, reconnect loop, and current
OMEMO behavior live in [bridges/xmpp-bridge](/home/cmc/ironclaw/bridges/xmpp-bridge).
Configured `rooms` are auto-joined by the bridge on connect.
Configured `encrypted_rooms` are treated as fail-closed encrypted groupchats:
they are validated as non-anonymous, members-only rooms, member/admin/owner
real JIDs are cached from MUC state, and plaintext groupchat traffic is ignored.

## Build

```bash
./channels-src/xmpp/build.sh
```

That produces `channels-src/xmpp/xmpp.wasm`.

## Install

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.ironclaw/channels
cp channels-src/xmpp/xmpp.wasm channels-src/xmpp/xmpp.capabilities.json ~/.ironclaw/channels/
```

## Configure

The channel expects these secrets:

- `xmpp_password`
- `xmpp_bridge_token` (optional)

The channel expects these setup fields:

- `xmpp_jid`
- `bridge_url`
- `dm_policy`
- `allow_from`
- `rooms`
- `encrypted_rooms`
- `allow_plaintext_fallback`
- `max_messages_per_hour`
- `resource`
- `device_id`
- `omemo_store_dir`

Use `ironclaw onboard`, the channel setup UI, or extension configuration flows
to persist them. `max_messages_per_hour` caps outbound XMPP sends per bot
instance; set it to `0` to disable the cap.

```
│       │   └── lib.rs               ← WASM channel source

│           ├── darkirc_adapter.py   ← IRC-to-HTTP bridge (Python, no deps)

├── .env                             ← Bootstrap config (DATABASE_BACKEND, LLM_*, etc.)

└── channels/
    ├── darkirc.wasm                 ← Compiled WASM channel (copied after build)
    └── darkirc.capabilities.json    ← Channel config (copied after changes)
```

## What Lives Where

| Thing | Location | When to touch |
|-------|----------|---------------|
| WASM channel source | `channels-src/darkirc/src/lib.rs` | Changing channel behavior |
| Capabilities JSON | `channels-src/darkirc/darkirc.capabilities.json` | Changing permissions, polling, allowlist |
| Adapter source | `channels-src/darkirc/adapter/darkirc_adapter.py` | Changing IRC behavior, message limits |
| Installed WASM | `~/.ironclaw/channels/darkirc.wasm` | Never edit directly — copy from build |
| Installed capabilities | `~/.ironclaw/channels/darkirc.capabilities.json` | Never edit directly — copy from source |
| IronClaw localhost patch | `src/tools/wasm/host.rs` line ~265 | Only if ironclaw repo is reset/updated |

## Build: WASM Channel Only (most common)

After editing `src/lib.rs`, `Cargo.toml`, or `darkirc.capabilities.json`:

```bash
cd ~/ironclaw/channels-src/darkirc
cargo build --target wasm32-wasip2 --release
cp target/wasm32-wasip2/release/darkirc_channel.wasm ~/.ironclaw/channels/darkirc.wasm
cp darkirc.capabilities.json ~/.ironclaw/channels/
```

Then restart ironclaw. No need to rebuild the main binary.

### Common build errors

**"current package believes it's in a workspace"**
```bash
echo '[workspace]' >> Cargo.toml
```

**"can't find library darkirc_channel"**
Make sure `Cargo.toml` and `src/lib.rs` are at the same level — not inside a `channel/` subdirectory.

**wit_bindgen path errors**
The path in `lib.rs` must resolve from `Cargo.toml` location to `~/ironclaw/wit/channel.wit`:
```rust
wit_bindgen::generate!({
    world: "sandboxed-channel",
    path: "../../wit/channel.wit",  // from channels-src/darkirc/ → wit/
});
```

## Build: IronClaw Binary (rare)

Only needed when patching IronClaw itself (e.g., the localhost HTTP fix in `host.rs`):

```bash
cd ~/ironclaw
cargo build --release
```

This takes a while. The binary lands at `~/ironclaw/target/release/ironclaw`.

### The Localhost HTTP Patch

IronClaw's WASM sandbox blocks plain HTTP. Our patch in `src/tools/wasm/host.rs` (~line 265) allows it for localhost:

```rust
let validator = AllowlistValidator::new(capability.allowlist.clone());
// Allow plain HTTP for localhost/loopback endpoints
let validator = if capability.allowlist.iter().any(|p| p.host == "127.0.0.1" || p.host == "localhost" || p.host == "::1") {
    validator.allow_http()
} else {
    validator
};
```

## 10. HTTP SECURITY NOTES

All extensions:
1. Use **localhost-only HTTP** (127.0.0.1 or localhost)
2. Include explicit HTTP allowlists in capabilities
3. Have secrets **injected by the host** at the HTTP boundary (WASM never sees raw credentials)
4. Use Bearer tokens, basic auth, or custom headers (X-Gotify-Key)
5. IronClaw patches its WASM sandbox to allow plain HTTP for localhost endpoints
